{{Short description|Mathematical graph for solving linear systems}}

[[File:Coates graph.svg|thumb|upright=1.3|The Coates graph of matrix A]]

In [[mathematics]], the '''Coates graph''' or '''Coates flow graph''', named after C.L. Coates, is a [[Graph (discrete mathematics)|graph]] associated with the  Coates' method for the solution of a [[system of linear equations]].<ref name="Swamy" /><ref name="Coates" />

The Coates graph ''G''<sub>''c''</sub>('''A''') associated with an ''n''&nbsp;×&nbsp;''n'' [[matrix (mathematics)|matrix]] '''A''' is an ''n''-node, weighted, labeled, [[directed graph]]. The nodes, labeled 1 through ''n'', are each associated with the corresponding row/column of '''A'''.  If entry ''a''<sub>''ji''</sub>&nbsp;≠&nbsp;0 then there is a directed edge from node ''i'' to node ''j'' with weight ''a''<sub>''ji''</sub>.<ref name="Chen" /> In other words, the Coates graph for matrix '''A''' is the one whose [[adjacency matrix]] is the [[transpose]] of '''A'''.
